messages:
sara (security): Heads-up — external compliance audit flagged possible unencrypted artifacts in last week's DB-to-objectstore backup job. They saw 3 object keys missing SSE headers in the sample. Can we collect evidence and triage?

maria (encops): On it. Which backup job id? I can pull uploader logs and S3 metadata.

sara (security): job id backup-2026-03-14-23Z. Auditor snippet attached in their report, says header missing: x-amz-server-side-encryption not present.

josh (infra): I pulled CloudTrail for PutObject around that time — majority show x-amz-server-side-encryption: AES256 or aws:kms, but there's a cluster of 3 PUTs from uploader-sa@prod with no SSE header. Could be older uploader binary not setting header.

li (sre): can you paste the CloudTrail entries? Also check KMS grant logs — maybe PutObject succeeded but metadata stripped during replication.

josh (infra): paste log:
```
{ "eventTime": "2026-03-14T23:12:03Z", "eventName": "PutObject", "userIdentity": "uploader-sa-prod", "requestParameters": { "x-amz-server-side-encryption": null, "key": "snapshots/db/tenant42/20260314.tar.gz" }, "responseElements": { "x-amz-request-id": "ABC123" } }
```

maria (encops): thanks. I also ran a head-object against that key — got headers showing no SSE header set. Head result:
```
ETag: "..."
Content-Length: 374827
x-amz-version-id: null
x-amz-server-side-encryption: <absent>
```

sara (security): Auditor is asking for timeline & controls. We should: 1) confirm if object was stored encrypted at rest (cloud provider may encrypt transparently), 2) verify KMS CMK usage & grants, 3) check uploader SA permissions and recent RBAC changes, 4) evidence package for auditor.

maria (encops): quick notes: AWS SSE-S3 is provider-managed; SSE-KMS uses our CMK. If head-object shows no SSE header, that likely means the object wasn't encrypted with SSE-S3/SSE-KMS at PUT time. But S3 does offer bucket default encryption — maybe PUT without header still gets SSE-S3 applied server-side. Need to check object-level encryption attribute in inventory or S3 metadata backend.

li (sre): I have S3 inventory enabled. Running a query now for that prefix and day. If inventory shows SSE-S3 for artifact, that suggests provider-side encryption was applied even without header.

josh (infra): KMS console: grants for our CMK were rotated on 2026-02-20. No grant gaps. But I see a failed Decrypt event for a separate access on 2026-03-15 — maybe unrelated.

maria (encops): Action plan: (A) collect CloudTrail PutObject + HeadObject + S3 inventory lines for the 3 keys; (B) export KMS GenerateDataKey/Decrypt logs for CMK; (C) snapshot uploader serviceaccount policy change history (IAM AccessAdvisor); (D) create evidence zip for auditors with signed statements.

sara (security): assign owners? Maria for A & C, Josh for B, Li for inventory query and timestamp verification. I'll prepare auditor-facing summary.

maria (encops): started collecting A & C. PR for RBAC rollback mitigation in progress — restricting uploader-sa to only PutObject with explicit sse parameter via condition: s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption = "aws:kms" OR require kms:EncryptionContext.

josh (infra): For B, KMS logs show GenerateDataKey happened for other services. For these specific PUTs there is no GenerateDataKey in CloudTrail (which aligns with no SSE-KMS usage). I exported the logs to /tmp/kms-audit-20260314.csv and uploaded to the compliance bucket (link: https://internal-redwood/s3/comp/kms-audit-20260314.csv ) :lock:

li (sre): Inventory query result: of 1.2k objects in that prefix, 3 show 'None' in SSE column. I'm attaching the CSV snippet below.

maria (encops): CSV snippet:
```
Key,SSE,Size
snapshots/db/tenant42/20260314.tar.gz,None,374827
snapshots/db/tenant99/20260314.tar.gz,None,129384
snapshots/db/tenant07/20260314.tar.gz,None,592103
```

sara (security): Good catch. Next steps: temporary mitigation = add an S3 bucket policy that denies PutObject when x-amz-server-side-encryption is null for our snapshots prefix. Maria, can you draft the policy and open an emergency PR? Tagging @oncall.

maria (encops): Drafted policy, PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4823 — includes deny unless sse header present and kms key id matches our CMK ARN. Requesting quick review.

audit-bot: Auditor request received: please upload evidence.zip to /compliance/incoming and provide who signed chain-of-custody. Reminder: attach CloudTrail exports and head-object outputs.

sara (security): Maria/Josh/Li, please assemble evidence.zip and post link here. Also prepare a short timeline and root cause hypothesis: oldest uploader binary didn't set SSE header; bucket default encryption not applied for this prefix in March because bucket default was added later (2026-03-20).

maria (encops): Evidence uploaded: https://internal-redwood/s3/compliance/evidence/backup-evidence-4198765432.zip — contains CloudTrail JSON, head-object outputs, KMS CSV, inventory CSV, PR diff. Signing chain: Maria -> Josh -> Sara.

li (sre): I also scheduled a small audit alert: if any new PutObject in snapshots prefix lacks SSE header, create PagerDuty incident and auto-block with bucket policy for 1 hour. Config PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-config/pull/129

josh (infra): FYI — I've added a short runbook in the PR describing how to revert bucket policy if it causes false positives. link: https://confluence.internal/redwood/encops/s3-sse-mitigation

sara (security): Thanks team. Auditor update drafted and sent. We'll follow up with longer-term fixes: uploader binary mandatory SSE-KMS flag, CI checks for backup artifacts, and nightly inventory diff alerts. Closing thread once auditor confirms receipt.

maria (encops): noted. Will monitor inventory job tonight and update here if any new 'None' entries appear.

li (sre): inventory finished — zero new negatives. Closing loop.

josh (infra): adding a note to infra changelog. :white_check_mark:

sara (security): great job. :thumbsup:
